newsitem.title: USA: ADM settlement gets preliminary approval.
newsitem.headline: ADM settlement gets preliminary approval.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co said Friday a federal judge granted preliminary approval of a settlement covering shareholder lawsuits against certain ADM directors which includes payment of $8 million by the directors to the company.
The shareholder derivative lawsuits alleged that certain current and former ADM directors did not prevent the activities that led to the company's 1996 guilty plea to price-fixing violations.
The defendant directors, without admitting liability, will pay $8 million to ADM to settle the claims, ADM said.

According to terms of the settlement, ADM directors also agreed to adopt certain corporate governance measures including a new definition of outside director, a new nominating committee for the 1997 board election, independent review responsibilities for the audit committee, confidential shareholder voting, and exclusive composition of the audit, compensation and nominating committees by outside directors.
Terms also call for dismissal of all derivative claims that shareholders have made in any court against the directors and ADM, the company said in a statement.
ADM keeps its claims against Mark Whitacre, Reinhard Richter, Sidney Hulse and Marty Allison. The company also keeps any claim which ADM may have against Michael Andreas and Terrance Wilson.
The settlement awards legal fees to the shareholders' lawyers, which will be paid out of the $8 million settlement proceeds.

U.S. District Court for the Central District of Illinois Judge Harold Baker granted preliminary approval of the settlement, ADM said. A final hearing on the terms will be held July 7, 1997 in Urbana, Ill.
ADM, a huge agricultural products processor, pleaded guilty last year to fixing prices of lysine and citric acid - a food additive - and paid a record $100 million in fines.
